paragraphs.text: Rome can be pricey for travelers, which is why many choose to stay in a hostel (旅社) . The hostels in Rome offer a bed in a dorm room for around 25 a night, and for that, you’ll often get to stay in a central location (位置) with security and comfort.
Yellow Hostel

If I had to make just one recommendation for where to stay in Rome, it would be Yellow Hostel. It’s one of the best-rated hostels in the city, and for good reason. It’s affordable, and it’s got a fun atmosphere without being too noisy. As an added bonus, it’s close to the main train station.
Hostel Alessandro Palace

If you love social hostels, this is the best hostel for you in Rome. Hostel Alessandro Palace is fun. Staff members hold plenty of bar events for guests like free shots, bar crawls and karaoke. There’s also an area on the rooftop for hanging out with other travelers during the summer.
Youth Station Hostel

If you’re looking for cleanliness and a modern hostel, look no further than Youth Station. It offers beautiful furnishings and beds. There are plenty of other benefits, too; it doesn’t charge city tax; it has both air conditioning and a heater for the rooms; it also has free Wi-Fi in every room.
Hotel and Hostel Des Artistes

Hotel and Hostel Des Artistes is located just a 10-minute walk from the central city station and it’s close to all of the city’s main attractions. The staff is friendly and helpful, providing you with a map of the city when you arrive, and offering advice if you require some. However, you need to pay 2 euros a day for Wi-Fi.

By day, Robert Titterton is a lawyer. In his spare  time though he goes on stage beside pianist Maria Raspopova — not as a musician but as her page turner. “I’m not a trained musician, but I’ve learnt to read music so I can help Maria in her performance.”

Mr Titterton is chairman of the Omega Ensemble but has been the group’s official page turner for the past four years. His job is to sit beside   the pianist and turn the pages of the score so the musician doesn’t have to break the flow of sound by doing it themselves. He said he became just as nervous as those playing instruments on stage.

“A lot of skills are needed for the job. You have to make sure you don’t turn two pages at once and make sure you find the repeats in the music   when you have to go back to the right spot.” Mr Titterton explained.

Being a page turner requires plenty of practice. Some pieces of music can go for 40 minutes and require up to 50 page turns, including back turns for repeat passages. Silent onstage communication is key, and each pianist has their own style of “nodding” to indicate a page turn which they need to practise with their page turner.

But like all performances, there are moments when things go wrong. “I was turning the page to get ready for the next page, but the draft wind from the turn caused the spare pages to fall off the stand,” Mr Titterton said, “Luckily I was able to catch them and put them back.”
Most page turners are piano students or up-and-coming concert pianists, although Ms Raspopova has once asked her husband to   help her out on stage.
“My husband is the worst page turner,” she laughed. “He’s interested in the music, feeling every note, and I have to say: ‘Turn, turn!’ Robert is the best page turner I’ve had in my entire life.”

When the explorers first set foot upon the continent of North America, the skies and lands were alive with an astonishing variety of wildlife. Native Americans had taken care of these precious natural resources wisely. Unfortunately, it took the explorers and the settlers who followed only a few decades to decimatea large part of these resources. Millions of waterfowl (水禽) were killed at the hands of market hunters and a handful of overly ambitious sportsmen. Millions of acres of wetlands were dried to feed and house the ever-increasing populations, greatly reducing waterfowl habitat.

In 1934, with the passage of the Migratory Bird Hunting Stamp Act (Act), an increasingly concerned nation took firm action to stop the destruction of migratory (迁徙的) waterfowl and the wetlands so vital to their survival. Under this Act, all waterfowl hunters 16 years of age and over must annually purchase and carry a Federal Duck Stamp. The very first Federal Duck Stamp was designed by J. N. “Ding” Darling, a political cartoonist from Des Moines, lowa, who at that time was appointed by President Franklin Roosevelt as Director of the Bureau of Biological Survey. Hunters willingly pay the stamp price to ensure the survival of our natural resources.

About 98 cents of every duck stamp dollar goes directly into the Migratory Bird Conservation Fund to purchase wetlands and wildlife habitat for inclusion into the National Wildlife Refuge System — a fact that ensures this land will be protected and available for all generations to come. Since 1934, better than half a billion dollars has gone into that Fund to purchase more than 5 million acres of habitat. Little wonder the Federal Duck Stamp Program has been called one of the most successful conservation programs ever initiated.

Popularization has in some cases changed the original meaning of emotional (情感的) intelligence. Many people now misunderstand emotional intelligence as almost everything desirable in a person’s makeup that cannot be measured by an IQ test, such as character, motivation, confidence, mental stability, optimism and “people skills.” Research has shown that emotional skills may contribute to some of these qualities, but most of them move far beyond skill-based emotional intelligence.

We prefer to describe emotional intelligence as a specific set of skills that can be used for either good or bad purposes. The ability to accurately understand how others are feeling may be used by a doctor to find how best to help her patients, while a cheater might use it to control potential victims. Being emotionally intelligent does not necessarily make one a moral person.

Although popular beliefs regarding emotional intelligence run far ahead of what research can reasonably support, the overall effects of the publicity have been more beneficial than harmful. The most positive aspect of this popularization is a new and much needed emphasis (重视) on emotion by employers, educators and others interested in promoting social well-being. The popularization of emotional intelligence has helped both the public and researchers re-evaluate the functionality of emotions and how they serve people adaptively in everyday life.

Although the continuing popular appeal of emotional intelligence is desirable, we hope that such attention will excite a greater interest in the scientific and scholarly study of emotion. It is our hope that in coming decades, advances in science will offer new perspectives (视角) from which to study how people manage their lives. Emotional intelligence, with its focus on both head and heart, may serve to point us in the right direction.

你校英文报Youth正在庆祝创刊十周年。请你写一篇短文投稿，内容包括：
1. 读报的经历；2. 喜爱的栏目；3. 期望和祝福。
注意：1. 写作词数应为80左右；
2. 请按如下格式写字答题卡的相应位置作答。
Youth and Me
阅读下面材料，根据其内容和所给段落开头语续写两段，使之构成一篇完整的短文。
A MOTHER’S DAY SURPRISE

The twins were filled with excitement as they thought of the surprise they were planning for Mother’s Day. How pleased and proud Mother would be when they brought her breakfast in bed. They planned to make French toast and chicken porridge. They had watched their mother in the kitchen. There was nothing to it. Jenna and Jeff knew exactly what to do.

The big day came at last. The alarm rang at 6 a. m. The pair went down the stairs quietly to the kitchen. They decided to boil the porridge first. They put some rice into a pot of water and left it to boil while they made the French toast. Jeff broke two eggs into a plate and added in some milk. Jenna found the bread and put two slices into the egg mixture. Next, Jeff turned on the second stove burner to heat up the frying pan. Everything was going smoothly until Jeff started frying the bread. The pan was too hot and the bread turned black within seconds. Jenna threw the burnt piece into the   sink and put in the other slice of bread. This time, she turned down the fire so it cooked nicely.

Then Jeff noticed steam shooting out of the pot and the lid starting to shake. The next minute, the porridge boiled over and put out the fire. Jenna panicked. Thankfully, Jeff stayed calm and turned off the gas quickly. But the stove was a mess now. Jenna told Jeff to clean it up so they could continue to cook the rest of the porridge. But Jeff’s hand touched the hot burner and he gave a cry of pain. Jenna made him put his hand in cold water. Then she caught the smell of burning. Oh dear! The piece of bread in the pan had turned black as well.

group-2021-i-reading-a.overview: 本文是一篇应用文（旅行指南），介绍了罗马四家青年旅社（hostel）供游客选择，先总述罗马住宿偏贵、旅社性价比高，再分条目逐一推荐各家旅社的特色。

discourseStructure.summary: 总-分结构：首段点明罗马住宿贵、旅社便宜划算的背景，随后以四个小标题分别介绍 Yellow Hostel、Hostel Alessandro Palace、Youth Station Hostel、Hotel and Hostel Des Artistes 四家旅社各自的优势与不足。

paragraphs.summary: 罗马对游客来说花费高，所以很多人选择住旅社；旅社一晚约25，且通常位置中心、有安全和舒适保障。
paragraphs.function: 引言/总述：交代背景，点明选择旅社的核心原因是便宜划算。

paragraphs.function: 分项标题：引出第一家旅社。

paragraphs.summary: Yellow Hostel 是城里评价最好的旅社之一，价格实惠、氛围有趣又不吵，且靠近主火车站。
paragraphs.function: 分项介绍：推荐 Yellow Hostel 的综合优势。

paragraphs.function: 分项标题：引出第二家旅社。

paragraphs.summary: Hostel Alessandro Palace 适合喜欢社交的人，工作人员办很多酒吧活动，夏天屋顶还有与其他旅客交流的区域。
paragraphs.function: 分项介绍：突出该旅社的社交氛围。

paragraphs.summary: 小标题：Youth Station Hostel。
paragraphs.function: 分项标题：引出第三家旅社。

paragraphs.summary: Youth Station 干净现代，家具床铺漂亮，不收城市税，有空调暖气，每个房间免费Wi-Fi。
paragraphs.function: 分项介绍：突出该旅社的整洁现代与诸多便利。

paragraphs.summary: 小标题：Hotel and Hostel Des Artistes。
paragraphs.function: 分项标题：引出第四家旅社。

group-2021-i-reading-b.overview: 本文是一篇人物报道，介绍律师 Robert Titterton 在业余时间担任钢琴家 Maria Raspopova 的翻谱员（page turner）的故事，讲述这份工作所需的技能、练习与偶发状况。

discourseStructure.summary: 文章按总—分结构展开：先引出人物及其特殊身份，再依次说明翻谱员的职责、所需技能、练习要求、突发状况，最后通过钢琴家夫妇的对比凸显 Robert 是优秀的翻谱员。

paragraphs.summary: 引出 Robert Titterton 白天是律师，业余时间为钢琴家 Maria 翻谱，并自述虽非专业音乐人但学会了读谱。
paragraphs.function: 引入人物与话题，点明翻谱员需要读谱能力。

paragraphs.summary: 介绍 Titterton 担任 Omega Ensemble 翻谱员四年，职责是坐在钢琴家旁翻谱，使演奏不被打断，他上台同样紧张。
paragraphs.function: 说明翻谱员的具体职责与心理状态。

paragraphs.summary: Titterton 解释这份工作需要诸多技能：不能一次翻两页，要在反复段落处找到正确位置。
paragraphs.function: 列举工作所需技能，体现其难度。

paragraphs.summary: 翻谱需要大量练习，长曲可达40分钟、翻页50次；台上无声沟通是关键，每位钢琴家有自己的点头示意方式需与翻谱员配合练习。
paragraphs.function: 强调练习的重要性，指出需练习识别点头示意。

paragraphs.summary: 如同所有演出，也会出岔子：一次翻页时气流把备用谱吹落，幸好他及时接住放回。
paragraphs.function: 用具体事例说明工作中的突发状况。

paragraphs.summary: 大多数翻谱员是钢琴学生或崭露头角的钢琴家，不过 Raspopova 曾让丈夫上台帮忙。
paragraphs.function: 过渡，引出钢琴家丈夫这一对比对象。

paragraphs.summary: Raspopova 笑称丈夫是最差的翻谱员，因他沉浸于音乐、感受每个音符而忘记翻页，并称 Robert 是她一生中最好的翻谱员。
paragraphs.function: 通过对比收尾，解释丈夫为何是最差翻谱员并赞美 Robert。

group-2021-i-reading-c.overview: 本文是一篇说明文，介绍美国联邦鸭票（Federal Duck Stamp）项目。先讲述北美水禽资源因捕猎与湿地破坏而锐减，再讲1934年《候鸟狩猎邮票法》出台、鸭票的诞生，最后说明鸭票收入如何用于购买湿地栖息地、成为最成功的保护项目之一。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按问题—对策—成效三段递进展开：第一段提出水禽资源遭破坏的问题，第二段介绍1934年法案与鸭票制度作为应对措施，第三段说明鸭票资金的去向与项目的巨大成效。

paragraphs.summary: 探险者与移民到来后，北美水禽与湿地资源在几十年内被大量破坏，市场猎人捕杀水禽、湿地被排干用于居住与耕种。
paragraphs.function: 提出问题：水禽资源锐减及其原因。

paragraphs.summary: 1934年《候鸟狩猎邮票法》出台，规定16岁以上猎人须每年购买并携带联邦鸭票，首张鸭票由Ding Darling设计。
paragraphs.function: 提出对策：以立法和鸭票制度保护水禽与湿地。

paragraphs.summary: 每一美元鸭票约98美分直接进入候鸟保护基金购买湿地与栖息地，自1934年以来已购买超过500万英亩栖息地，项目被誉为最成功的保护项目之一。
paragraphs.function: 总结成效：资金用途与项目的巨大成功。

group-2021-i-reading-d.overview: 本文是一篇议论性说明文，探讨情商（emotional intelligence）这一概念在普及过程中产生的误解，并辨析其真实含义，进而评价情商普及的整体影响，最后表达对未来情绪科学研究的期望。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文先指出情商被普及化后产生的误解（第一段），再给出作者更准确的定义即情商是一套中性的技能（第二段），接着评价普及的整体效果利大于弊（第三段），最后表达对未来科学研究的期望（第四段）。

paragraphs.summary: 普及化改变了情商的原意，很多人把情商误解为人身上一切无法用智商测试衡量的可取品质。
paragraphs.function: 提出问题：指出对情商的常见误解。

paragraphs.summary: 作者更愿意把情商描述为一套可用于善意或恶意目的的特定技能，举医生与骗子为例，说明情商高不等于道德高。
paragraphs.function: 界定概念：给出作者对情商的准确定义并举例说明。

paragraphs.summary: 尽管大众观念超前于研究所能支持的范围，但普及的整体效果利大于弊，使各方重新重视情绪的功能。
paragraphs.function: 评价影响：肯定情商普及带来的积极作用。

paragraphs.summary: 作者希望情商持续受关注能激发对情绪的科学研究兴趣，未来科学进步将提供研究人们如何管理生活的新视角。
paragraphs.function: 展望未来：表达对未来情绪科学研究的期望。

q-2021-i-032.questionFocus: 考查对情商常见误解的细节理解，定位第一段对误解内容的描述。

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它可以用智商测试来衡量。

trapEvidence.quote: that cannot be measured by an IQ test

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它有助于锻炼一个人的头脑。

trap.optionText: It includes a set of emotional skills.
trap.optionEntity: It includes a set of emotional skills
trap.explanation: 把情商描述为一套情感技能是作者本人的准确定义，而非题干所问的常见误解，对象张冠李戴。

trapEvidence.quote: We prefer to describe emotional intelligence as a specific set of skills

optionAnalysis.label: D

trap.explanation: 原文第二段是定义和举例，并未提出或解释任何规则，属于无中生有。

trap.explanation: 医生与骗子是为阐明“情商可用于善或恶”这一概念而设的对比例证，并非孤立地陈述某个事实，把举例说理弱化为单纯陈述事实。

trap.explanation: 举医生与骗子的例子是为说明当下情商的中性用途，没有对未来做任何预测，属于无中生有。

locationParaphrases.note: 选项 clarify a concept 对应原文先给出 describe ... as a specific set of skills 的概念，再用 doctor/cheater 举例加以阐明。

locationParaphrases.note: 题干 doctor 直接定位到原文 a doctor to find how best to help her patients，说明情商用于善意目的。
